Supraland Review: Showing how Tiny really can be Grand – GameSpace.com

Supraland Review: Showing how Tiny really can be Grand
User Rating: 9.5
Matt Keith April 25, 2019 PC
Facebook Twitter Reddit
Adventurers take note, there’s a new sandbox world for you to explore. So grab your swords and equip that armor because you’ll be diving head first into one of the most dangerous worlds you’ve ever experienced… inside an actual sandbox. Supraland, from developer Supra Games, offers players a unique take on adventure, exploration, and adventure. So grab that coffee, kick back and enjoy our Supraland review.
Set in a literal sandbox, Supraland is a first-person Metroidvania puz zle game. Taking on the role of a red guy, you’re tasked with figuring out why the neighboring blue village is bent on destroying your water supply. So with little more than a thirty-second intro you’re tasked with saving the red village from certain doom. Light on story, Supraland focuses instead on allowing players to explore, discover and puzzle their way to hidden upgrades, secret areas and unique ways to solve problems.
Visually Supraland offers a fun, light-hearted art style that allows it to remain relevant and timeless simultaneously. The world itself is creatively designed and immediately reminded me of the classic “ Honey I Shrunk the Kids”. It’s both sad and telling that I refer to that movie as a classic but the point is that Supraland offers a unique perspective on the world which in turn creates a fun and interesting world to explore.
Supra Games seems to have tried to balance the game mechanics between combat, puzzling and exploration attempting to not lean too heavily on any one of them. This is a very delicate balance to strike but I was pleasantly surprised at just how well the developer has managed to handle this tension. At no point did the game seem to lean too heavily on any one of the game mechanics but instead blended them all together nicely.
Combat is a straightforward affair with whatever weapon you have equipped simply striking whatever monster is in front of you. Through upgrades, both purchased and discovered, combat becomes a more complex and rewarding experience as you explore and puzzle your way through the world.
Puzzles in Supraland range from basic push this to activate this to more complex Goldberg style affairs requiring you to set up and execute complex chain reactions. Overall it’s a very rewarding experience in a similar vein to games like portal without being so complex that it halts the flow of the game. Completing puzzles rewards players with everything from coins (used to purchase upgrades) to story progression such as unlocking new areas or triggering key events.
Exploration is an extremely rewarding venture for players to partake in as much of the worlds little nooks and crannies offer some of the best rewards. Based on my play time most of these rewards come in the form of coin and upgrades and allow the player to access areas or meet interesting NPCs that you would otherwise miss altogether.
Speaking of NPC’s I would be remiss not to mention just how great the comedy is in Supraland most of which is delivered through the NPCs in the world. To avoid most of the spoilers I won’t give you any specific examples other than to say that I may have come across a very unique chemist in my travels. Suffice it to say, it’s worth taking the time to have a look around in each area as you are guaranteed to meet some very pop culture characters along the way.
Tags: exploration, FPS, metroidvania, Open World, puzzle
Summary
Supraland is a wonderful indie title that shows that a developer really can achieve anything with the right idea and creativity. The game promises 15-30 hours of exploration, puzzles, and combat and based on my play time I can say that this is a promise they will definitely deliver on. If you're looking for a unique take on the Metroidvania experience I can highly recommend checking out Supraland.

What is more, all of the puzzles become even more awesome considering the stylish, detailed, and high-quality graphics. There is no concrete plot in this title. You just find yourself in a gigantic world, where you can find thousands of adventures. Make decisions on your own and invent the story while you play. In Supraland, you are the author of the plot. There is a number of different paths on the map. Most of the paths are initially closed: to unlock them, you must find special objects and gain new abilities. These abilities need to be applied in different ways to make your character develop and get more capacities. The stronger you become, the more options open to you.
When creating puzzles, developers were inspired by Portal in many ways. At the same time, they tried to come up with unique tasks that cannot be found in other games. Each puzzle is extremely logical: as soon as you understand its essence, you can immediately solve it. Numerous enemies will try to prevent you from successful and calm puzzle solving. They will interfere you, so you will have to distract for fights. You have two different types of weapons to check out. These are melee weapons and ranged weapons (for example, you can fight with a sword or strike a monster with a rocket). The battles in this game are very dynamic. We bet that they will remind you about good old shooters, like Quake. Sometimes, solving puzzles and fighting at the same time won’t be an easy task. This might be even a bit annoying – you have almost got the clue and the solving is almost here, but all of a sudden – boom! The enemies pop out from nowhere and attack you furiously. You will have to keep yourself alarmed all the time. This won’t be a walk in the park!
Due to a large number of different locations and game options, you will have an access to a great number of missions. Each of them is created with special attention and some of them will even make you stuck for a day or two. The puzzles are not very simple or obvious, but they are never absurd or intuitive, like in some other puzzle-solving titles. Indeed, there is nothing more frustrating than a couple of days spent in tries to understand the logic and finally you do something pretty spontaneous and voila – the problem is solved. You won’t find anything like that in Supraland. Only logic, only interesting and well-thought tasks. As you have already understood, the number of these tasks is pretty large. You will spend 15-30 hours passing the game. What is more, you can always restart it and choose another direction, not similar to the one you took for the first time. There are many side-missions and puzzles that are not always obvious. So if 30 are not enough to let you enjoy Supraland to the fullest, you are welcome to play it over and over again.
